ambient_trade.text: Selling salt in {town} at a fair price today. Wagonloads go first to whoever pays on the spot.
Buying good wool in {town} for {gold} a bolt. Quality only, I can smell a damp bale from across the river.
Who is still hauling salt out of {town}? I will pay {gold} a sack and cover the wagon insurance myself.
Pyrgeti wool is trading near {gold} a bolt this week. Lekhvan buyers, move fast :)

encounter_trade_offer.text: {player}, you drive a hard bargain but I like you. {gold} for the salt and an escort to {town}, and I will throw in the spare horses.
{player}, is {gold} your final number? I have wagons waiting and a long, expensive road to {town} ahead of me.
{player}, I will deal with you, but only because the road to {town} is worse without a deal. {gold}. Take it or leave it.
Deal in principle, {player}. Give me {gold} and I will forget the three gates I paid at this morning.
{player}, I will call it square at {gold} and you can ride with my caravan to {town}. Cheaper than any road I know.

encounter_greeting.text: Good day, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}, carrying salt and wool. Your party is blocking my road, so kindly step aside, ser.
{player}! {persona} here, {my_faction}'s most reliable wool merchant. Walk with me a while, I have prices that will make you smile.
{player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. Every wagon I own is insured, and every lord who hurts my trade will hear about it. Step aside, ser.
Ser {player}, {persona} for {my_faction}. Roads are dangerous enough without armed parties on them. Let us both keep moving.

player_raided_my_village.text: {player} burned {village}. Lovely, now every wagon on that road costs me double insurance. Bad for business, bad manners.
{player}, you burned {village}. I forgave my ambush for a fair price on horses, so you can make this right with a fair price too.
Burned {village} and did not even leave a bill, {player}? That is poor trading, and my insurers are already sulking.
{player}, {village} is gone and so is the trade it fed. Pay for the damage and we can talk numbers again.
Another ash heap near {village}. My salt is stuck on the road and {player} is the reason. Fix it or stop it.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} at war with {enemy_faction}. Wonderful. Every wagon I own just got a new insurance premium.
War between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}, and the salt roads close before lunch. Someone owes me for the lost days.
{enemy_faction} wants a fight with {my_faction}? Fine, I will sell blankets to both armies by spring.
Which lord thought a war with {enemy_faction} would help trade? My caravans are still waiting at the gate.

peace_made.text: Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last. The wool roads may finally be safe to drive a wagon down.
{my_faction} and {faction} signed peace. Good news for trade, bad news for the men who sell swords.
Peace with {faction}, finally. Prices will dip a little, but my wagons will arrive in one piece, and that is worth it.
Ink is dry on {my_faction}'s peace with {faction}. I am already pricing new routes, so do not thank me yet.

released_by_player.text: {player}, you let me go without a ransom. I will remember that when your party needs salt at a good price.
Thanks to {player} for releasing me rather than ransoming. Good manners cost nothing, and I always pay my debts.
{player}, I appreciate the release. A ransom would have been a worse deal for both of us, so consider this a fair trade.
{player} let me go instead of asking for ransom. Not a friend yet, but I will not forget a fair deal.

beat_by_player.text: {player}, {troop_count} of my men went down and you took the field. Congratulations. Now let us discuss what the road repairs will cost you.
{player} beat my {troop_count} men in the field. Bad afternoon for business, but a good lesson in buying better guards.
{player}, {troop_count} men lost to you. Fair fight, I suppose. Next time I hire guards I may ask you for advice.
{player} won the field against {troop_count} of my troops. I am out a lot of coin today and my insurers are calling.
{player}, your {troop_count} lances beat mine fair and square. Lost wagons are the worst kind of loss, so let us talk terms.

whisper_beg_help.text: {player}, {enemy_faction} is pushing toward {fief} and my wagons are stuck inside. Help me hold it and I will make it worth your while.
{player}, I am losing ground near {fief} to {enemy_faction}. Send some men and name your price, and I will pay it.
{player}, my salt stores in {fief} are at risk from {enemy_faction}. Spare a few lances and I will cover your supplies for a season.
{player}, {fief} will fall to {enemy_faction} without help. I am no soldier, but I can pay well for a few swords.

ambient_complaint.text: Bandits on the road outside {town} again. I have insured every wagon and the insurers are starting to look nervous.
{rival} is undercutting every price in {town}. Selling below cost is not a market, it is a tantrum.
{faction} tolls on the salt road are eating my margins alive. Every wagon pays and nobody says thank you.
Who is still building roads with no guards? Half my caravan time goes to watching for ambushes near {town}.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain on the road between {town} and the coast again. Mud is the only thing growing faster than my wool prices.
Anyone know if the bridge at {village} is open? I want to move salt before the weather turns.
Lag is killing my caravan timing. I lost a whole pack of salt to a lag spike, so please, patience :)
Quiet week on the salt roads, which means cheap goods for those willing to haul. Who wants a cart ride to {town}?
